newsitem.title: PERU: Shell picks two groups for Camisea contract bid.
newsitem.headline: Shell picks two groups for Camisea contract bid.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell said Thursday it had chosen two foreign groups to submit proposals for the development of a project to bring gas from Peru's Camisea hydrocarbon fields to the capital Lima.

The two chosen groups were a consortium of the United States' Bechtel, Peru's COSAPI and Brazil's Odebrecht, and another consortium made up of the United States' Fluor Daniel, Peru's Grana y Montero and Argentina's Techint, Shell said in a statement.
"Both consortia have been invited to submit a design proposal for the development of a gas plant, pipelines to Lima and gas fractionation and liquid export facilities," the statement said.
Shell said the design competition will last around six months.
The company expects to award the first phase of the contract - a detailed design of the proposed development - by mid-1997.

Shell said it also expects to award the second phase of the contract - the design's implementation - "at the same time as the final investment decision for the Camisea project, currently timetabled for early 1998."
Oil giants Shell and Mobil signed a contract with the government in May that gives them the rights for two years to appraise Camisea's huge reserves with a view to developing them.
Shell is the operating partner of the project with a 57.5 percent share.

"We have selected leading companies to tender for the development of the infrastructure which would enable us to bring Camisea gas and liquids to Lima," said Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. managing director Alan Hunt.
The Camisea reserves, situated 310 miles (500 km) east of Lima, are estimated to hold 11 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 600 million barrels of natural gas liquids.

Shell, which plans to drill three exploratory wells starting next February to appraise the reserves, hopes to produce gas as early as 1999, but the full development project would bring gas to Lima around 2002.
Shell is working to establish a market for the gas amongst industrial companies in Lima.
If Shell and Mobil develop the Camisea project, it will last 40 years and become the largest foreign investment commitment in Peru at almost $3 billion.

The project also considers the option of supplying gas to fuel a new 600 megawatt (MW) power plant expected before 2000 ahead of the main development of the fields. Shell has chosen a U.S. group of International Generating Company (Intergen) and Community Energy Alternatives (CEA) to negotiate exclusively a gas sale and purchase contract for the possible plant.
